You can’t use this - “<” - the ‘less than’ or ‘snap’ in the ‘Comment’ box - - -

This is an old problem, and I’m expecting what has happened is you’ve tried to put a ‘snap/less-than’ sign in the transcript, probably after - - - |A,*
It removes everything that follows it. Some of us have resorted to the ‘*’ - asterisk instead, but you can also, as you’ll see above, put it in the ‘Subject’ header, which is limiting. You could write up to that point, put the line with the ‘snap’ in the header, and then continue to write the rest in ‘Comment’ - or just jurry-rig it by using the asterisk. Best of luck. I know the frustration of it, but in this space that sign is taken as an HTML tag…

↳ Posted by ceolachan on November 12th, 2004.

This isn’t “King George IV,” or “The Old King’s Reel”

Errik, this fabulous tune is actually called “The King’s Reel,” neither “King George IV” nor “The Old King’s Reel,” though all the tunes seems related. Believe me! You’ll see they are all slighly different tunes if you listen to Ashley MacIsaac playing the set: King George IV/ King George V/ The Old King’s Reel/ The King’s Reel.

As I said somewhere before, there is no such reel called “King George IV.” I believe Mairead Mooney mixed up the title of well-known strathspey with that of this tune “The King’s Reel” when learning them from the playing of Buddy MacMaster. It seems two tunes are often played together in Cape Breton.

So, please edit the details of the tune.

Thanks for another great tune. Keep posting!

↳ Posted by slainte on November 13th, 2004.

P.S. Seamus Egan recorded this tune on banjo with Eileen Ivers: it’s in “Cape Breton Set” in his solo album “A Week in January.” Cracking track!

↳ Posted by slainte on November 13th, 2004.

Yeah, I confirm the real name of the tune is “The King’s Reel.” It seems in the Athole Collection (1884) under the title: you will find the abc transcription of the tune through this page: http://www.flutesong.net/music/abc/index.htm I think the key signature should be Ador, but it’s basically the same as errik’s transcription.

Re: The King’s / George The Fourth / King George the IV / King George IV

I’m sorry to bring up the 20-year-old issue and I do appreciate slainte’s valiant attempts to keep the Tunes section clean and organised back in the day – but I think we can address that at this stage, now that the functionality allows for the tunes to have as many names as needed without messing up the search and submissions.😃

After doing just a bit of research, Cape Breton musicians do call this tune “The King’s Reel” – but it first appeared in several Scottish collections so it’s not the only “right name” for the tune! (Not that there’re any “the only right” names in the tradition – it would be the equivalent of saying that “King George IV” isn’t the right name for the strathspey because it was titled “King George IV’s *Welcome*” in the Athole Collection).

According to annotations in Andrew Kuntz’s Tunearch, the King’s reel has been published under the following titles in the Scottish collections of music alone:

– The Kings / The King’s Reel / Kings Reel (1884, 1887, 1986)
– George the Fourth Reel (1870, 1898, 1997)

…and has been recorded in various sources by all these names as well as “King George the IVth” and “King George IV” by musicians other than Altan.

Not Altan’s fault after all! Just another tale of variation in the tradition.

While I can’t be sure it was originally named after King George IV like the strathspey or the name got expanded on the way, it would appear quite fitting as the guy was a known patron of music and arts and led an extravagant lifestyle that everyone but the bohemian folks seem to have hated. He even played violoncello alongside Nathaniel Gow at his private parties, is there any surprise tunes were named after him?😃
